new_agent_audits.name: version_check
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests and all four source modules. Expected build-time authority is invoking the toolchain compiler selected by RUSTC (or rustc on PATH) with fixed --verbose --version arguments, without a shell, and reading RUSTFLAGS/CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS to check allowed compiler features. This assumes the caller's toolchain/environment is trusted, as Cargo itself does; output capture has no timeout/size limit. Other code parses and compares bounded integer version/date components and channel strings. Test-only filesystem access reads excluded static fixtures, not application data. No dependencies, own build script, unsafe code, network, installation, writes or autonomous work. This scoped safe-to-run review does not certify arbitrary hostile compiler executables, malformed version parsing or production security.

new_agent_audits.name: bitflags
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests and every production module, including complete macro templates, parser, iterators, traits and optional serde/arbitrary/bytemuck integrations. No build script or native code. Generated code implements primitive bit operations, transparent storage, finite flag lookup/iteration and formatting to caller-provided fmt::Write/serde destinations. Parser consumes input split by | and returns errors for empty/unknown/invalid hex flags. Macro recursion consumes supplied syntax; user expressions/attributes remain the caller's Rust code. Optional bytemuck unsafe marker impls require the underlying primitive Pod/Zeroable type and transparent internal wrapper; no executable unsafe blocks were found. No file/environment/socket/process APIs, constructors or background tasks. Resource use scales with caller input/iterators; this is not an audit of arbitrary caller traits or production parser correctness.

new_agent_audits.name: wasm-bindgen-shared
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests, build.rs and all four source modules. Build script reads only two fixed schema source files relative to CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, hashes their text and emits Cargo env/rerun directives; it also executes git rev-parse HEAD with fixed arguments and no shell to derive a version suffix. This is expected local build metadata access under a trusted Cargo/git environment; it writes no files and makes no network requests. Runtime code is no_std+alloc: finite schema macro data, identifier validation via unicode-ident, string construction/escaping and a byte-wise module hash. It stores JS/source text as data and does not evaluate it. No unsafe code, runtime I/O, installation or autonomous tasks. Tests only compare a fixed schema hash. Dependencies and downstream code generators require separate coverage.

new_agent_audits.name: errno
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests and all six source modules, including Unix, Windows, WASI, Hermit and unsupported-target branches. Expected authority is reading/writing the current thread's OS error slot and obtaining a system error description. Unix/WASI use strerror_r into a fixed 1024-byte stack buffer, errno-location FFI and UTF-8 valid-prefix conversion, relying on the OS/libc string contract. Windows uses GetLastError/SetLastError and FormatMessageW with FROM_SYSTEM|IGNORE_INSERTS into fixed stack buffers; decoded UTF-16 is copied into a bounded UTF-8 buffer. Hermit stubs return fixed values; unsupported targets fail compilation. Unsafe operations are limited to these OS buffer/pointer/string interfaces; no build script, file/socket access, process execution, installation or background work. This source review does not independently verify every platform's libc/Win32 ABI or replace native-platform tests.

new_agent_audits.name: phf_shared
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests and all three production source modules including optional ptrhash and unicase/uncased implementations. Code computes keyed hashes and table indexes, borrows caller values, and formats constants only to a supplied Formatter. PortableSipHasher delegates integer writes after endian normalization. The only unsafe block reborrows slices of one-byte u8/i8/bool as bytes with the same length/alignment and lifetime; it performs no writes. Empty/malformed caller-provided displacement/pilot/remap tables can panic and are not certified for hostile production input. Iteration is over caller data; no own build script, native code, constructors, environment, filesystem, sockets, processes or autonomous work. SipHash implementation and downstream generators require separate coverage.

new_agent_audits.name: phf_generator
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests, both production library modules and the gen_hash_test binary. Generation uses a fixed-seed in-memory fastrand generator, caller-provided hash callbacks, bucket/displacement search and caller-sized vectors. Optional ptrhash retries random seeds with bounded pilot searches and in-memory relocation; it does not obtain OS entropy. No unsafe code, build script, filesystem, environment, network, subprocesses or installation. Generation assumes a finite set of distinct build-time keys: duplicate/adversarial keys or callbacks can cause unbounded retry/CPU use, and oversized tables can panic or exhaust memory. Safe-to-run here covers controlled local build inputs, not hostile runtime key sets. The explicit benchmark binary generates one million strings only when the user runs it; it is not started during dependency builds. No cryptographic or production denial-of-service guarantee is claimed.

new_agent_audits.name: proc-macro-crate
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests and the complete production library. Explicit crate_name calls read CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/Cargo.toml and the workspace manifest located by Cargo, cache their modification timestamps in a Mutex/BTreeMap and parse TOML dependency names, treating TOML as data. Workspace discovery invokes the CARGO environment executable with fixed locate-project --workspace --message-format=plain and a single --manifest-path argument, without a shell. Returned paths and executable are trusted Cargo build-environment inputs; file and command output reads are not size/time bounded. No unsafe code, own build script, network, writes, installation or background tasks. This covers expected build metadata inspection, not arbitrary hostile Cargo executables or manifests chosen by an attacker outside the controlled fuzz build. toml_edit requires separate coverage.

new_agent_audits.name: memoffset
new_agent_audits.notes: Read package inventory, both manifests, build.rs and all four source modules including the complete macro templates. The build script only invokes autocfg compiler-version probes for fixed versions and emits fixed cfg names. With NymWrap's pinned Rust 1.100, offset_of variants delegate to core::mem::offset_of!, raw-field address creation uses addr_of!, and other macros perform layout/size calculations on caller-supplied Rust types. Legacy compiler branches using MaybeUninit/alignment pointers, address subtraction/offset_from and reference formation were inspected; they are not a certification of old compiler provenance/packed-field behavior. Caller base expressions are evaluated outside injected unsafe blocks and raw field macros require the documented valid base/type preconditions. No native code, filesystem/network access, installation, unrelated subprocesses or background tasks; compiler/environment authority belongs to the separately covered autocfg build dependency. No production memory-safety guarantee for arbitrary caller pointers is claimed.
